And the bilateral bead tic described above is a compositional default, not a decision: in 101, 249, 286, 323, 360, 397, 434 and 471 the two pale beads sit at exactly the vertical centre on both left and right, so the eye reads a horizontal axis before it reads the instrument. In the stress row, 360, 397 and 471 lose the subject entirely — the drawing shrinks to a small cluster below centre with three quarters of the frame empty.
critique.action: Bound occupancy: constrain the outer extent of all geometry to 0.80-0.92 of the frame half-width in neutral for every seed, which grows 286 and 397 and pulls 138 and 508 in. Establish one dominant element per frame by making the primary graduated ring 2x the stroke weight and at least 1.3x the radius of the next largest element, and cap all satellite beads at 0.18 of the primary radius so they cannot compete. Move the satellites off the horizontal axis as described under thumbnailSurvival.

critique.observation: Mixed. Two round-1 defects are genuinely gone: the pair of orphan horizontal segments crossing 175 neutral is no longer there, and the grey overdraw mush has largely cleared with the ink reduction. The clipping was not addressed and is now systematic rather than incidental. Seed 175's right-hand satellite chain is severed by the viewBox in all three states — in neutral a cream ring is cut in half at the right edge and a teal arc runs out with it, in recovery the same, in stress a teal arc is cut. On contact.png, 508 neutral has cream rings sliced at all four edges, 471 neutral is cut at the right, and the left-hand bead touches or crosses the frame edge in 101, 323 and 434. Two further things read as errors rather than as drawing. At the centre of 138 and 508 a dark asterisk knot forms where a dozen low-contrast strokes converge; it has no readable geometry and looks like a collision. And the near-equal-radius offset circle pairs in 360, 397 and 471 read as a plate printed twice slightly out of register, which is a printing fault, not a nested ring.
critique.action: Declare one margin and hold it: set a hard 5% inset on all geometry so no arc is severed by the viewBox, or push every bleeding element to at least 1.5x the frame so the crop reads as intentional. Half-in, half-out is the only option that reads as a mistake, and it is the one currently shipping on 175's satellite chain. Kill the centre knot by enforcing a minimum clear radius of 6% of the frame at the shared centre in 138 and 508, with no stroke permitted inside it except a single drawn hub. Enforce the 15% minimum radius separation named under briefFidelity so the double-printed look in 360, 397 and 471 cannot occur.

critique.observation: PASS, and the round-1 note was acted on. The teal's luminance is up enough that it now separates from the brown ground at 120px — on contact-thumb.png I can read the teal ring in 101, 175, 249, 286, 323, 360, 434 and 471, where before it vanished. Aged brass ochre, oxidised copper teal, cream vellum on a warm ink-brown ground is exactly the brief: warm metal against dark paper, and the ground carries the drawing without competing. Two things still keep the colour from doing hierarchical work. Brass, cream and teal are still deployed at the same stroke weight and roughly the same area, so there is no accent — three co-equal inks. And there is an unnamed fourth ink in circulation: the dull desaturated grey-brass used for the ghosted satellites in 101 neutral's left bead and 471's right-side circles. Against this ground it does not read as depth, it reads as a stroke that failed to print.
critique.action: Make brass the accent and restrict it: brass on the primary graduated ring, its ticks and the pointer only, at roughly 15% of total ink, with cream carrying the armature and teal carrying the orbits. Either delete the grey-brass ghost ink or push it to a deliberate 35-40% opacity of the brass hue so it reads as a receding plane rather than as a faded stroke — the current value sits close enough to the ground that it reads as a rendering failure in 101 neutral.

critique.observation: PASS, and this is the axis where round 1's requested fix landed cleanly. On states.png seed 101 keeps its brass hexagon and its right-hand satellite chain — the small brass hexagon and the tiny terminal ring — unchanged in size and position through all three states; 138 keeps its 6-fold rosette and its dashed teal inner ring; 175 keeps its six cream bearings with the paired dark dots; 212 keeps its hexagon-inside-hexagon-inside-hexagon core. The seed now owns the armature and the state owns only the orbit radius, which is exactly the separation that was asked for. No seed becomes a different object under drawdown.
critique.action: Preserve this split when the state mechanic is reworked into arc removal: keep ring count, radius ratio, inscribed polygon and satellite clock angle seed-owned and state-invariant, and let stress change only WHICH arcs are drawn and recovery only how far out the stack extends. Do not let the coming gap-and-drop logic remove a seed's identity carrier — in 101 that is the right-hand satellite chain, in 212 the nested hexagon core, in 175 the six bearings; those three must survive every stress frame intact.

critique.observation: PASS. Laid out on contact.png the twelve unambiguously read as one project: one palette with consistent role assignment (teal orbits, brass armature, cream bodies), one warm ink ground, one vocabulary of circle, hexagon and bead, and no outlier — even 286, the most distinctive frame, is built from the same three ingredients. The coherence is now better earned than in round 1, because the five families genuinely differ in structure while sharing the language. The caveat is that part of the cohesion is still coming from the repeated bilateral bead layout, which is a template default rather than a shared language, so fixing that must not be allowed to shatter the set.
critique.action: When the satellite clock angle is randomised and the flower-of-life layout retired, hold these four invariants fixed as the identity carriers: the shared centre, the palette-to-role mapping, the tick geometry (72 divisions, every sixth doubled), and the hairline-to-heavy stroke ratio. Vary counts, radii and angles; never vary the grammar.

critique.observation: GATE FAIL, and the frame is further from the brief than it was last round. The brief asks for concentric rings and dials, rings inside rings, engraved. The dominant mark on this sheet is no longer a ring at all -- it is a flat translucent SQUARE. Every one of the twelve neutrals on contact.png is a rosette of 10-14 overlapping quadrilaterals ringed around a solid cream disc: 101, 175, 249, 286, 323, 397 and 471 have no circle in them larger than the 40px satellite badge. A brief that says 'rings inside rings' has been answered with squares beside squares. Across all 36 frames on contact.png and states.png there is still not one tick, not one numeral ring, not one pointer, not one gnomon, not one vernier -- the third round running that nothing here was built to measure. The closest approach is the 12 small pale square nodes riding the hairline brass arc in 175, and they are rivets, not graduations: uniform length, no every-fifth emphasis, and lower contrast than the disc they sit on. 'Engraved' has gone backwards too: at 4x on 175 every element is a flat opaque or semi-transparent FILL with an anti-aliased edge and there is no hairline-against-heavy stroke contrast anywhere in the packet -- this reads as cut-paper collage, not as an engraved plate.
critique.action: Delete the square-rosette layer entirely -- it is the layer that broke the gate, and 175's twelve squares are the clearest instance. Rebuild the primary armature as 5 rings on ONE shared centre at radii 0.30 / 0.45 / 0.62 / 0.78 / 0.90 of the frame half-width, alternating stroke weight 0.75px hairline against 2.5px heavy so the ratio is at least 3:1. Graduate the 0.62 and 0.90 rings with 72 radial ticks each, 5px long and perpendicular to the ring, with every sixth tick doubled to 10px and drawn in brass. Add one brass pointer per token: a straight spoke from centre to the 0.90 ring ending in a filled triangle 8px wide. Promote the 40px satellite dial in 175 -- brass arc, teal ring, cream ring, brass hub on one centre -- to the primary subject at 4x its current size; it is the only genuinely nested, genuinely instrument-like object in 36 frames and it is currently a badge hanging off the side.

critique.observation: FAIL, and this is a regression that erased the one thing the last build delivered. The three files singles--seed175-neutral.png, -stress.png and -recovery.png are the same picture: I opened all three and they are indistinguishable, down to the position of every dark square and the clip on the teal satellite. On states.png at 3x magnification, seed 101 neutral / stress / recovery have the same 11 squares at the same radii with the same dark square at 10 o'clock, and differ only in the brightness of the brass connector stub and the position of two or three 2px specks; seed 175 is identical across all three. On states-thumb.png the three rows are the same row twelve times over. Nothing is cut away under stress -- no arc is severed, no ring dropped, no tick ladder truncated, nothing reads as incomplete anywhere in the twelve stress frames. Nothing opens outward under recovery -- element count and outer radius are unchanged. The teal-orbit-radius mechanic that made the state change legible at 120px in the previous build is gone and nothing replaced it.
critique.action: Restore a state mechanic and make it structural rather than cosmetic. For stress: erase 35-50% of each ring's circumference in 2-3 gaps of 40-70 degrees so rings render as open segments with visible cut ends, delete 2 of the 5 concentric rings outright and leave their radii empty so the hole in the stack is readable, and stop the tick ladder mid-run at a seed-chosen bearing. Hold the outer ring radius CONSTANT under stress so the wound is a hole in something whole. For recovery: freeze every neutral ring in place, forbid any new mark inside the neutral inner radius, and add 3 rings at 1.15x, 1.35x and 1.55x the neutral outer radius so ring count rises from 5 to 8. Test on states-thumb.png: 101 stress must be distinguishable from 101 neutral at 120px, which is false today.

critique.observation: FAIL, decisively, and worse than the previous build. On contact-thumb.png at 120px, eight of twelve seeds are one pale lump: 101, 175, 249, 286, 323, 397 and 471 are mutually indistinguishable cream blobs, and 434 is the identical blob rendered at roughly half scale. Only 138 and 508 read as a separate thing (dark ground carrying a cream star), and only 212 and 360 add anything else (a brass hexagon, a grey mottle). Twelve seeds resolve to about three looks -- down from the five families that were readable last round. The teal has also disappeared from browse size again: scanning contact-thumb.png I can find teal only in 138 and 212, because the teal orbit ring was replaced by a 15px badge that is below the resolution of the thumbnail. On states-thumb.png all three rows are the same row, so the 120px sheet carries no state information at all.
critique.action: Give each seed one silhouette-level decision that survives at 120px and holds through all three states: set concentric ring count per seed across 4 to 8, and outer radius across 0.55 to 0.92 of the frame half-width, both seed-owned and state-invariant. Restore teal to a full orbit ring at no less than 0.45 of the frame half-width so it occupies enough pixels to read at 120px -- the 15px badge in 175 is below thumbnail resolution and is wasted ink. Move the satellite dial off 3 o'clock: draw its clock angle from 12 positions 30 degrees apart, since all twelve seeds currently place it at exactly 3 o'clock and that shared right-hand nub is the strongest shape signal on contact-thumb.png. Target: any two of the twelve neutral frames distinguishable side by side at 120px, currently false for 101, 175, 249, 286, 323, 397 and 471.

critique.observation: FAIL, and a collapse from the previous build's five families back toward one recipe. Full size on contact.png I can name only three or four groups: cream square-rosette blob (101, 175, 249, 286, 323, 397, 471 -- seven of twelve, more than half the collection on one idea), dark ground with cream star (138, 508), brass polygon containing a blob (212, 434), and the grey mush (360). Within the seven-strong first group nothing structural varies: same square count within one or two, same radius, same centre, same right-hand satellite at the same clock position. 101 and 397 differ only in how many dark squares landed on the perimeter. 175 and 286 differ only in whether the cream disc is smooth or lumpy. The hexagram in 138 and the eight-point star in 508 are the same construction at two rotation counts.
critique.action: Cap any one family at 2 of 12 seeds -- the square-rosette family currently holds 7. Add two independent structural axes beyond density: vary the inscribed polygon across four values (triangle, square, hexagon, none) so 101, 175 and 397 cannot land on the same one, and vary the inner-to-outer radius ratio across 0.20 to 0.60 in steps so 249 and 286 separate by proportion rather than by surface texture. Make the satellite dial present in only about 60% of seeds instead of all twelve. Vary the 138/508 star point count across 5, 6, 8 and 12 rather than shipping the same hexagram twice.

critique.observation: FAIL. There is no focal hierarchy in nine of twelve frames because the largest, brightest element is also the emptiest: the central cream disc in 101, 175, 249, 286, 323, 397 and 471 is a flat undifferentiated field occupying roughly half the frame, so the eye lands on a void and finds nothing to read. 360 is the opposite failure -- roughly thirty stacked translucent squares with no dominant element at all. Frame occupancy still swings about 2:1 across neighbours on the same sheet: 434 neutral sits at roughly 45% of frame height with wide dead margins on all four sides, while 175, 286 and 471 run their star points off the top and bottom edges. 212 leaves the entire bottom third of its frame empty while the drawing sits high. And the satellite is at exactly 3 o'clock, at exact mid-height, in all twelve seeds, so every frame carries the same horizontal-axis reading before the instrument is read.
critique.action: Put something in the centre: make the innermost graduated ring at 0.30 radius carry visible structure -- a hub, a cross-hair, a numeral ring -- so the cream disc in 175 and 286 stops being a hole. Establish one dominant element per frame by making the primary graduated ring 2x the stroke weight and at least 1.3x the radius of the next largest element, and cap all squares and beads at 0.18 of the primary radius so they cannot compete. Bound occupancy: constrain all geometry to 0.80-0.92 of the frame half-width in neutral for every seed, which grows 434 and pulls 175, 286 and 471 in. Cut 360's stacked-square count from roughly 30 to no more than 10.

critique.observation: FAIL, and the clipping named in both previous rounds is now systematic and lands on the one element that satisfies the brief. The nested satellite dial -- brass arc, teal ring, cream ring, brass hub -- is severed by the right viewBox edge in 101, 138, 175, 212, 249, 286, 323, 360, 434, 471 and 508: eleven of twelve seeds. In 508 an entire brass-and-teal bracket chain is sliced through mid-component at the right edge and reads as a rendering failure. In 175 the whole satellite is cut roughly in half. Separately: 360 neutral is a flat grey-putty mat where the individual squares stop being readable as squares -- the overdraw fusion from round 1, returned and worse. In all three 175 frames a hard horizontal seam runs the full frame width at about 40% height and again at about 78%, the unmotivated top and bottom edges of a full-width translucent square, and it reads as banding. In 138 and 508 the main brass ring and a second brass ring sit offset by roughly 12% of radius, still reading as a plate printed twice out of register. And the three seed-175 single files are the same PNG shipped three times under three different state names.
critique.action: Declare one margin and hold it: set a hard 5% inset on all geometry so the satellite dial in 175, 212 and 508 is drawn whole inside the frame, or push it to at least 1.5x the frame so the crop reads as intentional -- half-in half-out is the only option that reads as a mistake and it is what ships in eleven of twelve seeds. Cap overdraw at 4 overlapping fills in any 8px radius to clear 360's grey mat. Remove the two full-width translucent squares producing the horizontal seams at 40% and 78% height in 175. Enforce a 15% minimum radius separation between any two primary circles so the double-printed offset in 138 and 508 cannot occur. Re-render the three seed-175 singles from their three actual states.

critique.observation: WEAK, and this axis lost the PASS it earned last round on two counts. First, the value structure inverted: cream now occupies the majority of the frame in 101, 175, 249, 286, 323, 397 and 471, so the warm ink-brown ground survives only as a thin border and the brief's 'warm metal against dark paper' reads instead as pale blob on a dark margin. Second, the teal shrank from a full orbit ring to a roughly 15px badge and has vanished at browse size again -- on contact-thumb.png it is findable only in 138 and 212. The desaturated grey-brass that was one ghosted stroke last round has grown into a dominant ink: 360, 249 and 471 read as grey and putty rather than as brass and copper, and against this ground that grey still reads as a fill that failed to print. Brass survives and is doing the best work in the packet -- the dashed ring in 138 and the hexagon in 212 are the two most convincing objects here.
critique.action: Invert the area budget: cap cream at 35% of frame area, currently above 50% in seven seeds, and let the ink-brown ground carry the majority so the metal reads against paper. Restore teal to a full orbit ring at 0.45 or more of the frame half-width so it survives 120px. Restrict brass to the primary graduated ring, its ticks and the pointer at roughly 15% of total ink, making it the accent rather than a co-equal third. Either delete the desaturated grey fill dominating 360 and 249 or push it to a deliberate 35-40% opacity of the brass hue so it reads as a receding plane.

critique.observation: WEAK, and it passes vacuously. Yes, seed 101 is recognisably 101 in all three states on states.png, and 138 keeps its dashed brass ring and hexagram, and 212 keeps its brass hexagon and nested hexagon chain. But that is not evidence of a preserved identity carrier -- it is a consequence of the three states being the same drawing, confirmed by the seed-175 singles being one identical file under three names. An axis that can only be satisfied by the state mechanic being absent has not been tested. Note also that the identity carriers themselves are thin: 101's carrier is a right-hand nub that all twelve seeds also have.
critique.action: Re-test this axis after the arc-removal state mechanic is restored, and protect three named carriers through every stress frame: 138's dashed brass ring, 212's nested hexagon chain, and 175's ring of 12 pale square nodes. Make ring count, radius ratio, inscribed polygon and satellite clock angle seed-owned and state-invariant, and let stress change only which arcs are drawn and recovery only how far out the stack extends.

critique.observation: PASS. Laid out on contact.png the twelve unambiguously read as one project: one palette with consistent role assignment, one warm ink ground, one vocabulary of translucent square, brass polygon and right-hand satellite, and no outlier -- even 360, the muddiest frame, and 508, the darkest, are built from the same ingredients. But this passes for the wrong reason, the same reason flagged in round 1: the cohesion comes from seven of twelve seeds being near-duplicates and from every frame carrying the identical 3-o'clock satellite nub, which is a template default rather than a shared visual language.
critique.action: Hold four invariants fixed as the identity carriers while the seedVariation and thumbnailSurvival fixes are executed: the shared centre, the palette-to-role mapping (teal orbits, brass armature and ticks, cream bodies), the tick geometry of 72 divisions with every sixth doubled, and the 3:1 hairline-to-heavy stroke ratio. Vary counts, radii and the satellite clock angle; never vary the grammar.

critique.observation: GATE FAIL. The brief asks for soft biological tissue under a microscope and forbids straight lines, repeating grid and nameable symmetry. Every one of the twelve frames is a mathematically perfect circle with a hard vector edge, and the only interior figure is either an axis-aligned crosshair (138, 175, 249, 286, 397, 471) or a 45-degree square/diamond (101, 212, 323, 360, 434, 508). Those are the two most nameable symmetries there are: 4-fold rotational and infinite rotational. Seed 212's stress frame adds hard-edged blue and violet RECTANGLES outside the disc. There are no cell walls, no lobes, and no wet edge anywhere in the packet: the disc boundary is a crisp constant-radius arc with zero perturbation. At 120px the object reads as a planet with moons, or as a rifle-scope reticle, not as tissue.
critique.action: Replace the circle primitive entirely. The silhouette must be a closed irregular boundary — polar radius modulated by 3-5 summed low-frequency noise octaves at roughly 15-30% radius amplitude, closed with cubic curves and never a straight segment — and its seed must drive the lobe count (3-7 lobes) so no two tokens share an outline. Delete the crosshair and the diamond outright; do not soften them. Substitute interior structure that is only ever curve-bounded: 8-20 non-convex Voronoi-ish cell compartments with 1.5-3px darker septa between them, walls meeting at irregular Y-junctions, no cell repeated and no two walls parallel. Nothing in the frame may be axis-aligned or 45-degree aligned; rotate every element by a seeded angle and forbid the renderer from emitting a straight-line segment longer than about 4% of the frame.

critique.observation: Twelve seeds are one work at twelve settings. The variables that actually move across the sheet are only three: disc radius (roughly 0.30 to 0.52 of frame), the count and clock position of 2-4 dark satellite discs, and a binary choice between cross and diamond. Silhouette, ground gradient, hue and internal structure are constant. 101/323/360 are the same picture at three sizes; 249/286/397 likewise. The brief explicitly required irregular silhouettes different on every token and this delivers one silhouette twelve times.
critique.action: Move the seed onto the shape grammar, not onto the transform of one shape. Target roughly 60-70% of the visual difference between two tokens coming from outline and cell topology (lobe count, lobe asymmetry, cell count, wall thickness, nucleus placement) and at most 30% from scale and satellite placement. Concretely: at least 4 distinct tissue morphologies rather than 2 motifs, and per-token variation in cell count of 3x or more end to end, so 101 and 323 stop being the same drawing.

critique.observation: On contact-thumb.png the twelve tiles collapse into one repeated stamp: a pale pink lozenge with two or three dark blobs stuck on its rim. The interior figure — the only element that distinguishes half the collection from the other half — is the first thing to disappear, because the crosshair and the diamond sit at roughly the same lightness as the disc they are drawn on. I can separate 434 (smallest) and 508 (largest) at 120px; the middle eight are interchangeable. The dark satellite blobs are the only high-contrast marks in the frame, so at browse size they, not the subject, are what the eye reads.
critique.action: Raise interior-structure contrast against the disc body by roughly 2.5-3x in value (the septa should be the darkest marks inside the membrane, currently they are among the lightest) and simultaneously cut the satellite blobs' contrast against the ground by about half, or drop them. Then re-render the 120px sheet and require that twelve tiles be sortable into at least six visually distinct groups by outline alone with the interior blurred out.

critique.observation: Half the claim is weakly delivered and half is not delivered at all. Neutral to stress produces a visible change in only about 4 of 12 seeds at browse size — 212 gains blue rectangles, 434 gains a magenta rim ring, 101's diamond enlarges, 138 gains a scatter of blue glyphs — while 249, 286, 323, 397, 471 are essentially unchanged between the top two rows of states-thumb.png. Worse, stress to recovery is invisible in all twelve seeds at both 512px and 120px: on seed 175 the recovery frame differs from the stress frame only by a few pixels of satellite drift. The brief says recovery should let the tissue settle, and nothing settles — the recovery row is the stress row.
critique.action: Make both transitions structural rather than decorative, and make them opposite in sign. Stress: swell the outline by 12-18% with the lobes losing definition (blend the boundary noise toward a rounder, tighter form), thicken the septa by about 1.6x, push hue about 15-25 degrees toward hot magenta-red and raise saturation about 30%, and blur the edge to read as wet and turgid. Recovery: return outline scale to within about 3% of neutral, restore lobe definition and septum thickness to roughly neutral values, and desaturate back to about 10% above neutral — leaving only a residual scar cue so recovery is not a pixel copy of neutral either. Success test: with labels hidden, a viewer must sort the three rows of states-thumb.png into the correct order at 120px.

critique.observation: There is a focal hierarchy — one dominant disc — but it is inert. The disc is centred with near-equal dead margin on all four sides in every seed, and the frame is used only as a container. The internal figure often sits off-centre from the disc for no legible reason (175's crosshair is centred while a second, smaller crosshair plus a scatter of dots sits to its lower right, reading as leftover debris rather than a second nucleus). The lower third of the frame is empty in every token.
critique.action: Break the centring: offset the membrane centroid by 8-15% of frame width on a seeded angle, and let the tissue run off one or two edges in about a third of the tokens so the frame reads as a crop of a slide rather than a portrait of an object. Give the off-centre secondary cluster an actual role — make it a nucleus with a real membrane and a size relationship (about 0.15-0.25 of the parent lobe) — or delete it.

critique.observation: The hue family is consistent and clearly chosen, but it is doing almost no work. Range is compressed into a narrow dusty rose to mauve band, so the interior figure is only a few values away from the body it sits on and vanishes at browse size. The haematoxylin blue the brief asks for exists only as a handful of stray specks and glyphs (138, 175, 212) that read as dirt, never as a nuclear stain. The warm smoky brown-violet ground gradient competes with the drawing rather than supporting it: it lightens toward the bottom of the frame until the disc's lower edge dissolves into it (clearest on 249 and 286).
critique.action: Promote haematoxylin blue from speck to structural register — nuclei and septa in deep blue-violet at roughly 25-35% lightness, occupying about 10-15% of the tissue area, against pink cytoplasm at 65-75% lightness. Widen the working value range from its current roughly 20 points to about 55. Flatten the ground to a near-neutral faint cytoplasm grey with no more than about 8 points of gradient, and make sure it is darker than the membrane's lightest passage everywhere so no edge dissolves.

critique.observation: Real defects, by location. Satellite discs are cut by the viewBox rather than composed against it: top-right of 286 and right edge of 508 on contact.png each lose a disc to the frame, and on singles seed 175 the left-hand dark disc is sliced by the left edge in all three states. On 175 the cluster of tiny pink and blue dots plus a half-scale crosshair to the right of centre reads as a mistake — elements colliding into speckle with no size or spacing logic. On 138 stress and recovery the blue x and + glyphs sit OUTSIDE the disc at its upper-left, floating on the ground with nothing to attach to, which reads as a spill. Several disc edges vanish where they cross the ground gradient's light band (249, 286, 397 lower edge).
critique.action: Either inset all elements so nothing is cut, or commit to the crop and let elements cross the edge by at least 25% of their own diameter so the cut reads as intentional rather than as clipping — never the current 5-10% nick. Bind every satellite and every glyph to the membrane geometry (attached to a lobe or inside a compartment) so nothing floats free on the ground. Remove the sub-scale dot scatter entirely, or give it a minimum mark size of about 1.5% of frame and a Poisson-disc spacing so it reads as granulation instead of noise.

critique.observation: This axis passes, and it passes for the wrong reason. Laid out on contact.png the twelve unmistakably belong to one project — but the shared identity is a single reused primitive rather than a shared visual language. The risk on the next revision is real: the fixes above widen variation substantially, and the thing holding the set together right now is exactly the thing that has to go.
critique.action: Before widening the seed space, fix the identity in properties that survive the rewrite: the stained-slide ground, the pink-cytoplasm-plus-blue-nucleus two-register palette, the septum weight ratio, and the wet edge treatment. Those four should be invariant across all twelve tokens while outline, cell topology and scale all move freely.

critique.observation: GATE FAIL, and it is the same failure as last round with the hue rotated. The brief asks for soft tissue under a microscope with cell walls, irregular lobes and a wet edge, and forbids straight lines and any nameable symmetry. All twelve tokens are still a perfect constant-radius circle: zooming the left rim of seed 175 neutral at 4x shows a clean antialiased arc with zero boundary perturbation, no feathering, no lobes, no septa. The interiors are worse than last round, not better: seed 175 is a large 45-degree square plus three smaller squares with dead-straight edges running 200+ px; seeds 249 and 434 carry regular hexagons; seed 434's stress state IS a regular pink hexagon, six straight edges and 6-fold rotational symmetry, presented as the inflamed state; seeds 138 and 508 are literal compass roses with a straight crosshair bar spanning the full frame width and four X/+ glyphs in 180-degree rotational pairs. Seeds 101, 323 and 360 are concentric circles, which is infinite rotational symmetry. At 120px the sheet reads as planets with moons and as surveyor's reticles. There is not one cell wall, one lobe or one wet edge anywhere in the packet.
critique.action: Delete the circle, the square, the diamond, the hexagon and the crosshair from the shape vocabulary entirely rather than restyling them; forbid the renderer from emitting any straight segment longer than 4% of frame width and any regular polygon. Build the silhouette as a closed polar boundary with radius modulated by 4 summed low-frequency noise octaves at 18-30% radius amplitude, seeded lobe count 3-7, closed with cubic curves only. Fill it with 10-20 non-convex curve-bounded compartments separated by 2-3px septa meeting at irregular Y-junctions, and rotate every element by a seeded angle so nothing is axis- or 45-degree aligned.

critique.observation: Stress is now visible on some seeds and recovery is not delivered at all. On states-thumb the neutral-to-stress transition moves 15-26% of pixels on 101, 138, 175, 212, 323, 360 and 508, but only 4-6% on 249, 286 and 397, which are indistinguishable between the top two rows. Stress-to-recovery is 4-10% on every seed, which in this collection is the satellite-drift noise floor: on seed 175 at 512px the stress and recovery frames differ inside a single bounding box at x302-388, y84-436 - the right-hand satellite column - and 0.96% of pixels; the membrane and every square inside it are pixel-identical. Measuring the pink area on seed 138 gives 3.44% neutral, 9.01% stress and 9.01% recovery to two decimals, and on 212 it is 0.00 / 4.15 / 4.23, so where recovery moves at all it moves FURTHER from neutral. Nothing settles. Separately the stress cue is wrong in kind: elements scale up uniformly and 212 and 434 gain a hard-edged pink outline ring, which reads as a zoom and a machined trim rather than inflammation.
critique.action: Make the two transitions structural and opposite in sign. Stress: swell the outline 12-18%, blend the boundary noise toward a rounder tighter form so lobe definition drops, thicken septa 1.6x, push hue 15-25 degrees toward hot magenta-red, raise saturation about 30% and soften the boundary by 2-3px so it reads wet and turgid. Recovery: return outline scale to within 3% of neutral, restore lobe definition and septum thickness to neutral, desaturate to about 10% above neutral, and leave a residual scar so it is not a copy of neutral either. Then require that stress-to-recovery move at least 15% of pixels on every one of the twelve seeds on the 120px sheet, and that the three rows of states-thumb be sortable into the correct order with labels hidden.

critique.observation: On contact-thumb the twelve tiles sort into exactly three groups: eight indigo discs each wearing one pink blob at 1-2 o'clock and one at 5 o'clock on the rim (175, 212, 249, 286, 323, 397, 434, 471), two discs with two dark dots that read as a face (101, 360), and two compass roses (138, 508). Every interior figure vanishes at 120px, because the interior sits about 9 lightness points from the body it is drawn on - measured on 175 neutral, disc body luminance 0.29 against diamond 0.38. The two pink satellites are the highest-contrast marks in the frame, so at browse size the eye reads the accessories and not the subject, which is exactly the round-1 finding recoloured.
critique.action: Raise interior-structure contrast against the membrane body from its current ~9 lightness points to 30-35 points, making the septa the darkest marks inside the membrane, and cut satellite contrast against the ground by half or drop the satellites. Then re-render the 120px sheet and require that the twelve tiles be sortable into at least six visually distinct groups by outline alone with the interiors blurred out.

critique.observation: Twelve seeds, three moving variables: disc radius (about 0.32 to 0.55 of frame), which interior stamp is used (concentric ring / diamond / hexagon / compass rose), and satellite count. Silhouette is a circle on 12 of 12, so the one thing the brief said must differ on every token is the one thing that is identical on every token. Seeds 101 and 323 are the same drawing - same disc size and position, same concentric inner circle, same satellite at 1 o'clock carrying the same small companion dot, same satellite at 5 o'clock with the same pale twin - differing only in where two small dark dots sit. 249, 286, 397 and 471 are one picture at four scales. Mean tile colour across all twelve lies inside RGB (72-96, 63-77, 89-99), a band 24 points wide, so no seed has a colour identity either.
critique.action: Move the seed onto the shape grammar rather than onto the transform of one shape: target 60-70% of the difference between two tokens coming from outline and compartment topology (lobe count 3-7, lobe asymmetry, compartment count varying 3x end to end, septum weight, nucleus placement) and at most 30% from scale and satellite placement. Ship at least 4 distinct tissue morphologies instead of the 4 interchangeable interior stamps, and add a build check that refuses the set if any two of the twelve outlines match within 5% of their radius profiles - 101 and 323 must stop being the same drawing.

critique.observation: The colour is now doing less work than last round, not more, and the two registers have swapped the wrong way. On seed 175 neutral the ground gradient spans about 46 lightness points from 0.10 at the top of the frame to 0.56 at the bottom, while the entire drawing spans about 9 points (disc body 0.29, its main diamond 0.38): the background carries all the tonal range and the subject carries none. Haematoxylin blue has swallowed the whole cell body on 10 of 12 tokens, so the deep nuclear blue is now the cytoplasm and the stained-slide pink survives only as two rim satellites and, on 138 and 508, as the compass diamond. Faint cytoplasm grey is absent. The ground still lightens toward the bottom until the disc's lower edge dissolves into it on 249, 397 and 471.
critique.action: Invert the two registers back: pink cytoplasm at 65-75% lightness as the body, deep blue-violet nuclei and septa at 25-35% lightness occupying 10-15% of tissue area. Widen the drawing's own value range from about 9 points to about 55 while cutting the ground gradient from about 46 points to no more than 8, and hold the ground darker than the membrane's lightest passage everywhere so no edge dissolves. Give each seed a hue offset of at least 12 degrees from its neighbours so the twelve tile means stop sitting inside a 24-point RGB band.

critique.observation: All twelve frames are the same arrangement, not twelve compositions: one disc near frame centre with roughly equal dead margin on all four sides, one pink satellite at 1-2 o'clock on the rim, one at 5 o'clock, and an empty bottom third. On 286 the disc's top is sliced flat by the frame across about 8% of its diameter, so the only frame interaction in the whole set is an accident. The interior figure is 9 lightness points from the body and therefore subordinate to the two satellites, which means the compositional accent is on the accessories.
critique.action: Break the template: offset the membrane centroid by 8-15% of frame width on a seeded angle, and let the tissue run off one or two edges by at least 25% of its own width on about a third of the tokens so the frame reads as a crop of a slide. Randomise satellite clock position across a full 360 degrees instead of the fixed 1-o'clock/5-o'clock pair, or bind the satellites into the membrane as daughter compartments at 0.15-0.25 of the parent lobe and delete the free-floating ones.

critique.observation: Real defects, by location. On 286 the large disc is cut flat across the top by the frame - a chord about 8% of its diameter, too small to read as an intentional crop. On 508 the horizontal crosshair bar runs edge to edge and is cut by both the left and right frame edges, while the upper X and the upper-right + are cut by the top edge and the lower X and + by the bottom edge. On 138 the same horizontal bar simply stops in mid-air about 25px short of each edge with no terminus. On seed 175 in all three states the blue squares at the diamond's upper-left and lower-left overlap it half-transparently with no size or spacing logic, and a 6px lone square floats at the disc's upper-left attached to nothing. The pale companion circles on the satellites (249, 286, 397, 471, 508) straddle the satellite rim at arbitrary angles and read as a duplicate-paste error. On 249, 397 and 471 the disc's lower edge disappears into the ground gradient's light band.
critique.action: Either inset every element so nothing touches the frame, or commit to the crop and let elements cross by at least 25% of their own diameter - never the current 8% nick on 286 or the ambiguous mid-air stop on 138. Bind every satellite and every glyph to the membrane geometry so nothing floats on the ground, delete the sub-scale stray squares under 2% of frame width, and give the companion circles a fixed anchoring rule (fully inside the parent, at 0.2-0.3 of its radius) instead of the current rim straddle.

critique.observation: The set does read as one project, but for the same weak reason as last round and now with two outliers. Coherence rests on one reused primitive plus one fixed satellite arrangement, so ten tiles cohere by being near-clones, while 138 and 508 sit outside the family entirely - no membrane at all, just a crosshair and glyphs on a bare gradient. That is 10 duplicates plus 2 strangers, not a shared visual language.
critique.action: Fix identity in four properties that survive the shape rewrite and hold them invariant across all twelve: the stained-slide ground, the pink-cytoplasm-plus-blue-nucleus two-register palette, the septum-to-body weight ratio, and the wet-edge treatment. Then bring 138 and 508 inside that language by giving them a membrane of their own and deleting their crosshair and glyph clusters, rather than leaving two tokens whose only shared property with the other ten is the background gradient.

critique.observation: This axis passes. Across neutral, stress and recovery each seed stays unmistakably the same token: on 175 the disc, its position, the four squares and both satellites persist across all three states, and on 212 and 434 the added rim ring and hexagon sit over an otherwise unchanged object. It passes partly because so little changes - the identity is never at risk when stress-to-recovery moves under 1% of pixels.
critique.action: Hold this property while implementing the marketResponse fix: after the stress and recovery transitions are made structural, keep compartment count, nucleus placement and the seeded lobe-count identity constant across all three states, and let only outline scale, septum weight, saturation and edge softness move, so the token stays the same object while genuinely swelling and settling.

critique.observation: GATE FAIL, third round, same failure with a new primitive. The circle was not replaced by an organic boundary — it was swapped for a right-pointing isoceles TRIANGLE, which is on 10 of 12 tokens, and the old primitives were kept alongside it. Zooming the left rim of seed 175 neutral at 6x shows a dead-vertical, one-pixel-hard boundary running 150px with zero perturbation and zero feathering; its hypotenuse is a ruler-clean diagonal about 270px long. The live shape vocabulary across the sheet is: isoceles triangle (101, 175, 212, 249, 286, 323, 360, 397, 434, 471), 45-degree rotated square (101, 212, 323, 360, 471), regular hexagon (434, 508), concentric circles (508), full-frame crosshair (138, 175, 286, 508), X and + glyphs, small axis-aligned squares, and on 286 a literal L-shaped register/crop mark at upper right. Every one is a nameable, ruler-drawn primitive; 434 is a regular hexagon (6-fold rotational) and 138 and 508 are surveyor's reticles with 180-degree rotational X pairs. There is still not one cell wall, one lobe or one wet edge anywhere in the packet, and the only non-geometric mark in twelve tokens is a roughly 10px pink scribble at 138's centre.
critique.action: Stop substituting one regular polygon for another. Delete triangle, rotated square, hexagon, circle, crosshair, X, + and the L register mark from the emitter entirely, and add a build assertion that refuses any straight segment longer than 4% of frame width (about 20px at 512) and any shape with more than 1 axis of mirror symmetry. Build the silhouette as a closed polar boundary: radius modulated by 4 summed low-frequency noise octaves at 18-30% radius amplitude, seeded lobe count 3-7, cubic curves only, no vertex where two segments meet at a fixed angle. Fill it with 10-20 non-convex curve-bounded compartments separated by 2-3px septa meeting at irregular Y-junctions, and feather the outer boundary by 2-3px so it reads wet. Nothing in the frame may be axis-aligned or 45-degree aligned.

critique.observation: Twelve seeds, three moving variables: triangle scale (about 0.30 to 0.55 of frame), which interior stamp sits on it (diamond / small squares / cross / hexagon / concentric ring), and satellite triangle count. Laid side by side at full size, 101, 323 and 360 are the same drawing — same right-pointing isoceles triangle, same inscribed 45-degree diamond, same pink nub at the left vertex, same satellite triangle upper-right and lower-right — differing only in whether the diamond contains two small squares (101), one small triangle (323) or one large plus one small square (360). 249, 286, 397 and 471 are one picture at four scales. The one property the brief said must differ on every token, the silhouette, is identical on ten of twelve.
critique.action: Move the seed onto the shape grammar rather than onto the transform of one shape: target 60-70% of the visual difference between two tokens coming from outline and compartment topology (lobe count 3-7, lobe asymmetry, compartment count varying 3x end to end, septum weight, nucleus placement) and at most 30% from scale and satellite placement. Ship at least 4 distinct tissue morphologies instead of 5 interchangeable interior stamps, and add a build check that refuses the set if any two of the twelve outlines match within 5% of their radius profiles — 101, 323 and 360 must stop being the same drawing.

critique.observation: On contact-thumb the twelve tiles sort into exactly three groups: eight blue right-pointing triangles that read as a media-player play button (101, 175, 249, 286, 323, 360, 397, 471), two pink polygons carrying a small blue triangle (212, 434), and two crosshair reticles with no body at all (138, 508). Every interior figure vanishes at 120px, because on seed 175 neutral the triangle body sits at luminance 0.228 and its brightest interior mark, the pink cross bar, at 0.375 — and the pink satellite triangles outside the body are the highest-contrast marks in the tile, so at browse size the eye reads the accessories and the frame reads as an icon, not as tissue. This is the round-1 and round-2 finding with the primitive changed.
critique.action: Make the septa the darkest marks inside the membrane and raise interior-structure contrast against the body to 30-35 lightness points (currently about 15 on 175), then cut the free-floating satellites' contrast against the ground by half or bind them into the membrane. Re-render the 120px sheet and require that the twelve tiles be sortable into at least six visually distinct groups by outline alone with the interiors blurred out, and that no tile read as a play arrow or a reticle.

critique.observation: Stress is now visible on most seeds and recovery is still not delivered at all. On states-thumb, neutral-to-stress moves 7-14% of pixels on 101, 212, 249, 323, 360, 434, 471 and 508 — a real gain over round 2 — but only 2-3% on 138, 175, 286 and 397. The stress cue is wrong in kind: seed 212 across its three states is a uniform ~1.9x zoom of the entire assembly, pink diamond, blue triangle, inner square and both satellites scaling together with identical proportions, and the added inflamed element is a hard-edged 45-degree rotated square with four ruler-straight 200px edges. That reads as a zoom and a machined trim, not as swelling. Stress-to-recovery moves 0.18% to 1.14% of pixels on all twelve seeds at 120px — invisible. An amplified difference of seed 175 stress against recovery at 512px shows the ONLY changes are the outlines of the two satellite triangles at (280-340, 70-130) and (275-340, 380-440) shifting 1-2px plus two tick glyphs; the triangle, the crosshair and every + glyph are pixel-identical. And on every one of the twelve seeds the neutral-to-recovery distance exceeds the neutral-to-stress distance (101: 8.87 vs 8.31; 212: 9.45 vs 9.33; 471: 14.69 vs 14.28), so where recovery moves at all it moves FURTHER from neutral. Nothing settles; the tissue keeps swelling.
critique.action: Make the two transitions structural and opposite in sign, and stop scaling the assembly uniformly. Stress: swell the OUTLINE 12-18% while holding satellites and interior glyphs at neutral scale, blend the boundary noise toward a rounder tighter form so lobe definition drops, thicken septa 1.6x, push hue 15-25 degrees toward hot magenta-red, raise saturation about 30% and soften the boundary by 2-3px. Recovery: return outline scale to within 3% of neutral, restore lobe definition and septum thickness to neutral, desaturate to about 10% above neutral, and leave one residual scar so it is not a pixel copy of neutral either. Then require that stress-to-recovery move at least 15% of pixels on every one of the twelve 120px tiles, that neutral-to-recovery be SMALLER than neutral-to-stress on all twelve, and that the three rows of states-thumb be sortable into the correct order with labels hidden.

critique.observation: The two registers are still inverted and the ground still outweighs the drawing. On seed 175 neutral the ground gradient runs from luminance 0.076 at the top of the frame to 0.437 at the bottom, a 36-point span, while the entire drawing spans 26 points (0.154 to 0.416) — so the background is the widest tonal event in the frame and at the bottom edge it is LIGHTER than the drawing's brightest passage, which is why the triangle's lower edge dissolves into the ground on 249, 397 and 471. Haematoxylin blue is still the cell body, not the nucleus: the triangle body reads deep indigo at 0.228 on ten of twelve tokens, and the stained-slide pink survives only as rim satellites, the cross bar and the 434/508 polygons. Faint cytoplasm grey is absent from the packet. Colour identity per seed is now worse than last round, not better: the twelve neutral tile means all sit inside RGB (74-80, 60-63, 72-78), a band 6 points wide, so no seed has a colour of its own.
critique.action: Invert the registers: pink cytoplasm at 65-75% lightness as the body, deep blue-violet nuclei and septa at 25-35% lightness occupying 10-15% of tissue area. Widen the drawing's own value range from 26 points to about 55, cut the ground gradient from 36 points to no more than 8, and clamp the ground darker than the membrane's lightest passage at every row so no edge dissolves. Give each seed a hue offset of at least 12 degrees from its neighbours so the twelve tile means stop sitting inside a 6-point RGB band.

critique.observation: Ten of twelve frames are the same arrangement rather than twelve compositions: one triangle near frame centre pointing right, roughly equal dead margin on all four sides, one pink satellite triangle upper-right, one lower-right, and an empty bottom quarter. The interior stamp sits about 15 lightness points from the body and is therefore subordinate to the satellites, so the compositional accent lands on the accessories. The two exceptions are worse, not better: 138 and 508 are dead-centre reticles with two-fold rotational symmetry about the frame centre, which is the most measured composition available and the opposite of what the brief asks for. The frame is a container everywhere; nothing is cropped deliberately.
critique.action: Break the template: offset the membrane centroid by 8-15% of frame width on a seeded angle, and let the tissue run off one or two edges by at least 25% of its own width on about a third of the tokens so the frame reads as a crop of a slide rather than a portrait of an object. Randomise satellite clock position across a full 360 degrees instead of the fixed upper-right/lower-right pair, or bind the satellites into the membrane as daughter compartments at 0.15-0.25 of the parent lobe and delete the free-floating ones. Delete the centred reticle layout on 138 and 508 outright.

critique.observation: Real defects, by location, most of them carried over unrepaired. On 138 the horizontal crosshair bar stops in mid-air about 40px short of the left frame edge and about 50px short of the right with hard rectangular termini attached to nothing, and the vertical bar does the same at top and bottom; on 508 the same bar stops about 25px short of the left edge. On 286 a sub-scale dark glyph at roughly x=152 of the tile is clipped by the top frame edge into a sliver, and a small L-shaped register mark sits at upper right belonging to no object. On 471 a cluster of four pink rotated squares at the lower right overlaps itself half-transparently with no size or spacing logic. On seed 212 stress and recovery the two satellite triangles are half-occluded by the added pink diamond and poke out at its top and bottom vertices, reading as a z-order accident. On 249, 397 and 471 the triangle's lower edge disappears into the ground gradient's light band.
critique.action: Either inset every element so nothing touches the frame, or commit to the crop and let elements cross by at least 25% of their own diameter — never a mid-air terminus 25-50px short of the edge, and never the sub-scale sliver clipped at 286's top. Bind every satellite and glyph to the membrane geometry so nothing floats on the ground, delete stray marks under 2% of frame width including 286's L register mark, and give 471's overlapping square cluster a Poisson-disc spacing with a minimum mark size of 1.5% of frame or remove it. Clamp the ground darker than the drawing at every row so no lower edge dissolves.

critique.observation: The set does read as one project, but for the same weak reason as the two previous rounds and with the same two outliers. Coherence rests on one reused primitive plus a fixed satellite pair, so ten tiles cohere by being near-clones, while 138 and 508 sit outside the family entirely — no body at all, just a crosshair and X glyphs on a bare gradient, sharing nothing with the other ten but the background. That is ten duplicates plus two strangers, not a shared visual language, and the identity currently holding the set together is exactly the primitive that has to be deleted.
critique.action: Fix identity in four properties that survive the shape rewrite and hold them invariant across all twelve: the stained-slide ground, the pink-cytoplasm-plus-blue-nucleus two-register palette, the septum-to-body weight ratio, and the wet-edge feathering width. Then bring 138 and 508 inside that language by giving each a membrane of its own and deleting their crosshair and X-glyph clusters, rather than leaving two tokens whose only shared property with the other ten is the background gradient.

critique.observation: This axis passes. Across neutral, stress and recovery each seed stays unmistakably the same token: on 175 the triangle, its position, the crosshair and both blue + glyphs persist across all three states, and on 212 and 434 the added diamond and hexagon sit over an otherwise unchanged object. It passes cheaply, though — identity is never at risk when stress-to-recovery moves under 1.2% of pixels on every seed.
critique.action: Hold this property while implementing the marketResponse fix: after the transitions are made structural, keep compartment count, nucleus placement and the seeded lobe-count identity constant across all three states, and let only outline scale, septum weight, saturation and edge softness move, so the token stays the same object while genuinely swelling by 12-18% and then settling back to within 3% of neutral.

critique.observation: The brief asks for a figure where what you see at the outside is what you see at the centre, smaller. In seeds 138, 249, 286, 397 and 508 there is no second generation visible at all — one large pale ellipse or square with loose gold confetti scattered around it. Only 323 (hexagons built of hexagons) and 434 (triangles built of triangles) actually recur on themselves. Half the collection does not read as nested.
critique.action: Raise the guaranteed floor to 3 drawn generations in the neutral state on every seed, and scale each child to 0.45-0.55 of its parent so the repeat is legible rather than implied. Delete the single-shape fallback path that produces the empty frames of 286 and 397.

critique.observation: "Colour should step outward level by level so depth reads as colour" is undelivered everywhere. Every interior is one flat milky pewter — in 175 neutral the entire inner tracery is invisible grey-on-grey — and colour is assigned by shape class instead of by level: gold on the outside ring, undifferentiated grey inside. Depth reads as nothing.
critique.action: Assign a per-level colour ramp of at least 4 stops running copper at generation 1 to pewter at generation 4, and force at least a 15% lightness gap between adjacent levels so the step survives at 120px.

critique.observation: The largest and highest-contrast mass in 9 of the 12 tiles is a soft-edged, axis-aligned pale grey panel that is not part of the figure and is not radial. In 175 and 286 it buries the drawing completely and the tile reads as a blank card on indigo. The brief asked for a rosette, an emblem, a stamped seal; what dominates the sheet is a rectangle.
critique.action: Cut the panel opacity by about 60% or remove it and let the deep indigo ground carry the figure directly. If a plate is kept, make it radial — a disc, or the figure's own base polygon — never an axis-aligned rectangle.

critique.observation: Focal hierarchy is inverted. The brightest, most saturated marks — the gold diamonds ringing 175 neutral, the gold hexagons ringing 212 neutral — sit at the outermost ring, while the centre is the emptiest and lowest-contrast area of the frame. The eye is pulled off the middle of a form that is supposed to be a stamped seal. Seeds 249, 360 and 101 are additionally off-centre, so the radial read is lost twice over.
critique.action: Restrict the gold accent to the innermost 2 generations and raise centre contrast against the panel by roughly 30% so the middle becomes the strongest point. Re-centre the figure on the frame centroid for 101, 249 and 360; the current offset reads as a bug, not a decision.

critique.observation: At 120px, seeds 175, 286 and 397 read as plain grey squares with no discernible figure, 101 reads as a grey square with a ghost of a hexagon, and 249 reads as an off-centre pile of grey rectangles that looks like a rendering error. That is 5 of 12 tiles that do not survive browse size. The interior tracery — the recursion, which is the whole subject of the brief — vanishes entirely in every tile because it is grey-on-grey.
critique.action: Raise minimum stroke width to about 2.5px at 512 (roughly 0.6px at 120) and require every level to hold at least a 20% value gap against whatever sits behind it. Then re-render the thumb sheet and gate on all 12 tiles showing a readable silhouette before anything else is judged.

critique.observation: Under stress, 138 and 508 gain three to four solid saturated gold discs in a horizontal row across the middle that appear in neither their neutral nor their recovery frame; 212 stress gains a solid gold block in its centre; 249 stress gains three yellow bars. At 120px the stress tile of 508 is not recognisably the same token as its neutral tile — it has been replaced by a different object rather than thinned.
critique.action: Forbid new shape classes in the stress state outright: restrict drawdown to removing generations and reducing element count. Cap total accent area in stress at or below the neutral accent area, and disallow solid fills on the accent in any state where they do not appear in neutral.

critique.observation: The stress row is instantly distinguishable at 120px, so the transition is visible — but it is visible by the wrong signal. The loudest change is added solid gold, not cut generations. Thinning does happen (175 stress and 101 stress genuinely drop levels), yet it is the quieter half of the change. In the other direction, recovery is effectively absent on 286 and 397, whose recovery tiles differ from their neutral tiles by one small orange square.
critique.action: Make drawdown drop 2 full generations and recovery add 2 on every seed, then verify that drawn-element count moves monotonically stress < neutral < recovery for all 12 seeds. Strip the stress-only gold discs so thinning is the only stress signal.

critique.observation: A pair of hard-edged grey slabs bleeds off the mid-left and mid-right of the pale panel in all three states of 175 and in 101, 138, 249 and 508 — they read as a rectangle clipped by mistake, not a design element. Frame clipping is heavy and uncontrolled: 101 recovery cuts hexagons at the left and bottom edges, 175 recovery cuts gold squares at all four edges, 138 stress cuts the outermost gold discs at both side edges, 212 recovery cuts at top and right. In 249 the overlapping opaque rectangles collide into mush with no readable figure underneath.
critique.action: Clamp the outermost generation's radius to 0.92 of the half-frame so nothing crosses the viewBox in any state, and delete the two mid-edge slabs entirely. Re-run 249 with opaque-rectangle stacking disabled.

critique.observation: The figure families are genuinely different where they work — 434 (triangle star), 323 (hexagon field), 360 (circles) and 212 (hexagon ring) are four different works, not one work rotated. But 138 and 508 collapse into the same look at 120px (pale ellipse, two dark flanking lobes, gold points on the rim), as do 360 and 471 (copper ring, pale circles, grey square), so 4 of 12 seeds resolve to 2 appearances, and 286 and 397 are near-empty.
critique.action: Widen the base-polygon draw so no more than 2 of 12 seeds share a base figure, and add branching-count variation across at least 3 distinct values (for example 5, 6 and 8 arms) so two seeds in the same family still separate at browse size.

critique.observation: The twelve do read as one project — but the thing holding them together is the pale grey panel and the gold confetti, not the nesting rule. Remove the panel and 286, 397 and 249 share nothing with 434. The coherence is carried by the same element that is the composition failure, so fixing the composition would currently dissolve the family.
critique.action: Move the coherence onto the rule instead of the plate: enforce the same generation ramp and the same copper-to-pewter level ordering on all 12 seeds, then re-render the contact sheet with the panel removed and confirm the family still reads.

critique.observation: GATE FAILS. The brief's subject is a figure that repeats its own rule inward — 'what you see at the outside is what you see at the centre, smaller'. In the majority of tiles what is actually drawn is a single opaque gold polygon with ornament scattered around its rim: 286 neutral is one flat gold hexagon with a 40px dark hexagon at its centre and nothing between; 101 is a flat gold hexagon with a pale hexagon ring hanging off its left side; 397 is a flat gold hexagon with a dark hole; 508 and 138 are flat gold blobs ringed by orange discs. Those five have no second generation visible inside the body at all. Where recursion does exist (175, 434, 323, 212, 471) it is drawn gold-on-gold inside the plate at roughly 8% value separation, so the nesting is a faint scribble rather than the subject. The frame reads as 'gold coin with confetti', not 'rosette built of itself'.
critique.action: Delete the opaque fill on the base polygon in all 12 seeds — render generation 1 as a stroked outline only — and draw a guaranteed minimum of 4 generations inside it, each child at 0.50-0.55 of its parent radius, so the nest is the body of the figure rather than a texture on top of a disc. Kill the single-solid-shape path that produces 286 and 397.

critique.observation: Focal hierarchy is still inverted, exactly as in round 1 — only the plate changed colour from pewter-grey to gold. In 101, 212, 286, 397 and 471 the centre of the frame is the emptiest, flattest region (a plain fill, or a single dark hexagonal hole) while every stroke, ring and diamond of interest sits on the outer rim. In a stamped seal the centre should be the strongest point and it is the weakest one in 5 of 12. Radial centring is broken as well: 138, 249 and 508 sit visibly off the frame centroid with their spray of orange discs weighted to one side, and 101's pale hexagon ring appears on the left and lower-right only, so the figure has no rotational read at all.
critique.action: Move the highest-contrast marks to the innermost 2 generations and raise centre-versus-plate contrast by about 30%; drop outer-rim accent density by about 40%. Re-centre 101, 138, 249 and 508 on the frame centroid and force the outermost generation's element placement to full rotational symmetry (5, 6 or 8 arms) so no seed keeps a one-sided ring.

critique.observation: The brief asks for deep indigo, warm copper, cold pewter and one accent that appears RARELY, with colour stepping outward level by level so depth reads as colour. The indigo ground is right and it does support the drawing. Everything after that is not delivered: the gold accent is the single largest area in 11 of 12 tiles (roughly 40-60% of the frame in 175, 286, 397, 508), so the rare accent has become the field; copper survives only as a thin outline ring and as loose discs; pewter is a few thin white strokes; and a fourth unbriefed hue — a violet-purple, most visible in the 175 recovery squares and in 323 — has been added, which sits badly against the copper. Depth still reads as nothing: inside 175 neutral, generations 2, 3 and 4 are all the same gold, so colour is assigned by shape class (orange rings, violet squares, white squares, gold body) rather than by level.
critique.action: Cap total gold coverage at 15% of frame area per tile and re-assign colour by GENERATION, not by shape class: a 4-stop ramp running copper at generation 1 to pewter at generation 4 with at least a 15% lightness gap between adjacent stops, gold reserved for generation 4 only. Remove the violet hue entirely — it is a fourth metal the brief never asked for.

critique.observation: The round-1 instruction that no more than 2 of 12 seeds share a base figure was not delivered: 101, 212, 286, 323 and 397 are all hexagon-based — 5 of 12 — and 138, 249 and 508 are all the same rounded blob with an orange disc spray. Only 434 (six-point star of triangles), 360 (concentric circles with white circle confetti) and 175 (eight-point octagon star) are unmistakably different FIGURES. At 120px the twelve resolve to about three appearances: 'flat gold hexagon with a dark centre' (101, 212, 286, 397, 323, 471), 'gold blob with orange dots' (138, 249, 508), and the two genuine outliers. Branching count does not vary visibly either — almost everything is 6-fold.
critique.action: Redraw the base-polygon draw so no more than 2 of 12 seeds share a base figure — retire 3 of the 5 hexagons in favour of pentagon, square-diamond and octagon bases — and vary the branching count across at least three distinct values (5, 6, 8 arms) so 286 and 397 separate from 212 at browse size.

critique.observation: Real improvement here and it should be kept: at 120px every one of the 12 tiles now has a readable silhouette against the indigo, where in round 1 five tiles read as plain grey squares. The gold-against-indigo value gap is doing that work. But the second question on this axis fails — at 120px the twelve do not look like twelve things (see seedVariation), and the SUBJECT does not survive at all: in 10 of 12 thumbs the interior nesting is invisible because it is gold-on-gold, so what browses is a flat gold shape. 249 at 120px is still an unreadable smudge of gold, navy and orange with no figure under it.
critique.action: Keep the gold-vs-indigo silhouette contrast, then force every generation to hold at least a 20% value gap against whatever is directly behind it and raise minimum stroke width to about 2.5px at 512 (0.6px at 120), so at least 3 generations are countable in the thumb. Re-render 249 with opaque-shape stacking disabled and gate on all 12 thumbs showing a countable nest before anything else is judged.

critique.observation: Direction is now correct and the round-1 defect is fixed — stress genuinely removes outer generations and recovery genuinely adds them, and the progression stress < neutral < recovery is legible at 120px on 101, 175, 212, 323, 360, 434 and 471. 175 stress is the cleanest frame in the whole packet. But three seeds deliver nothing: 286 neutral, 286 stress and 286 recovery are indistinguishable at 120px (the same flat gold hexagon in all three), 508 is likewise unchanged across its three rows, and 397 changes only by gaining a handful of small squares in recovery. That is 3 of 12 where the transition is invisible on the sheet.
critique.action: Force every seed to drop 2 full generations under stress and add 2 under recovery, then verify drawn-element count moves strictly monotonically stress < neutral < recovery for all 12 seeds — 286, 397 and 508 currently do not move and must be re-rendered until their three thumbs differ.

critique.observation: This axis is fixed. Across all 12 seeds on states-thumb.png every stress and recovery frame is recognisably the same token as its neutral frame — the base figure, its orientation and its colour assignment all hold. The round-1 defect where stress introduced solid saturated gold discs into 138, 508, 212 and 249 that existed in neither neutral nor recovery is gone: no new shape class appears in any stress frame, and drawdown now reads purely as thinning. 175's three states are unambiguously one object at three densities.
critique.action: Preserve the current rule that stress may only remove generations and element count — keep the ban on new shape classes and on solid accent fills in stress when applying every other change below.

critique.observation: Frame clipping is still uncontrolled on the worst seeds. 508 bleeds off the right and bottom of its tile with orange discs cut at all four edges in neutral, stress AND recovery; 138 is cut at the right edge in all three states; 249's confetti is cut top and left; 101 recovery has hexagons cut at the right edge. Separately, the round-1 mid-edge slabs were recoloured rather than deleted — three opaque dark navy hexagonal lobes now sit on top of the figure at roughly 10, 3 and 7 o'clock in all three states of 175, and the same navy blobs appear as soft ellipses smeared across the gold in 138 and 249, where they read as dirt on the render rather than as a design element.
critique.action: Clamp the outermost generation's radius to 0.92 of the half-frame in every state so nothing crosses the viewBox — re-render 508, 138, 249 and 101 recovery and confirm zero cut elements. Delete the three dark navy lobes in 175 and the navy ellipses in 138 and 249 outright; they are the round-1 slabs in new colour.

critique.observation: The twelve unmistakably read as one project on the contact sheet — but for the second round running the thing binding them is the failing element, not the rule. Remove the flat gold plate and the copper outline ring and 286, 397 and 508 share nothing with 434. The coherence is now so tight that it costs identity: six tiles are the same gold hexagon at different confetti densities, which is coherence and variation failure reading as the same picture.
critique.action: Move the binding onto the recursion rule — enforce the same 4-stop copper-to-pewter generation ramp and the same child-scale ratio on all 12 seeds — then re-render the contact sheet with the gold plate removed and confirm the family still reads before restoring any fill.

critique.observation: The brief forbids a centred emblem and forbids radial symmetry. Eleven of the twelve neutral frames are exactly that: a bilaterally symmetric stack that tapers in from wide bands at top and bottom to a pinched waist at mid-frame, with a knot or starburst of white blades sitting on the vertical centre line. In 175, 323 and 471 the white strokes converge on a single point near the middle of the frame, which is radial focus by construction. The subject a viewer names is not a drill core; it is a totem or an hourglass with an explosion in its middle. Seed 397 is the one frame that reads as the brief — full-width horizontal beds of varying thickness, no centre knot, no taper — which proves the target image is inside this runtime's reach and is being suppressed by the centring rule and the blade layer.
critique.action: Kill the taper and the centre attractor. Give every bed an independently randomised left and right edge in the range 0.0-1.0 of frame width instead of a width centred on 0.5, so band ends stagger and no vertical axis of symmetry forms; require at least 60% of beds to touch one frame edge. Move the white-line origin off the centre: draw them as near-horizontal rules with slope within about +/-8 degrees spanning edge to edge, not as a bundle radiating from an interior point. Target seed 397's read as the collection default, not as its outlier.

critique.observation: The cold half is genuinely chosen and it works: the glacial blue, slate and wet-shale beds sit in a tight, deliberate value band and the blues read as one family across all twelve seeds. The failure is the ash. The brief asks for a thin seam of pale ash; what renders is near-white at close to full luminance in blades 10-20px wide that are the brightest and largest objects in most frames, so the loudest thing in the picture is the one element the brief described as thin. Separately, the background gradient runs dark at the top to pale grey-blue at the bottom, which lightens the frame as it descends and inverts the depth logic of a core, so the ground fights the reading it is supposed to support.
critique.action: Drop the ash from near-white to a pale grey-blue and cut its brightest value by roughly 30-35% so it sits above the palest bed but below blowout, and cut stroke width by about 60% so it reads as a seam rather than a plank. Flip the ground gradient so the bottom of the frame is the darker end, or flatten it to a near-uniform slate; the vertical wash is currently doing more work than the beds.

critique.observation: There is a focal hierarchy, but it is pointed at the wrong subject and it is centred. The upper corners of nearly every frame are empty dark ground, the mass sits in a middle third, and the eye lands on the white knot rather than on the bedding. The bottom-most bar in several frames (175 neutral, 138 recovery, 212 neutral) sits detached at the very bottom edge with a gap above it, so it reads as a stray element rather than as the deepest bed in the sequence.
critique.action: Push bedding out to fill roughly the top 90% of the frame height rather than the middle third, and remove the gap under the lowest bed so the sequence is continuous to the bottom edge. Reduce the white layer's total ink by about 50% so that the beds, not the blades, are the first thing read.

critique.observation: The variation is bimodal and both failure directions are present on one sheet. At full size and at 120px, seeds 138, 175, 212, 249, 286, 434 and 471 read as the same stamp: blue horizontal stack, small white scribble at centre. That is seven of twelve near-interchangeable. At the other end, 360 and 508 are fans of white blades sweeping from the left edge that read as a wing or a broom, with the beds almost entirely obliterated, and 101 and 323 are white tangles with no legible stratigraphy at all. So four frames are off-project while seven are one project repeated.
critique.action: Narrow the top end and widen the middle. Cap the white element at roughly 25-30% of frame area so no seed can become a fan, and put the freed variance into the beds themselves: vary bed count across seeds by at least 3x (say 6 to 20), vary individual bed thickness across a 5x range within a frame, and vary the horizontal offset of each bed independently. The differentiator should be the bedding pattern, which currently barely varies, not the blade count, which currently varies too much.

critique.observation: At 120px on the contact sheet the horizontal banding does survive and the blues hold together, which is the good news. But the seven-frame middle cluster collapses to one repeated icon at that size: a blue striped block with a grey smudge in the centre. 360 and 508 survive as distinctly different things only because they have abandoned the strata. So browse size shows two icons and two oddities rather than twelve works.
critique.action: Since bed pattern is what survives at 120px, make it the carrier of seed identity. Force each seed to a recognisable bedding signature at thumbnail scale - a few dominant thick beds versus many fine laminations, top-heavy versus bottom-heavy mass, one bright seam versus three - and verify by viewing the contact sheet at 120px only. Aim for no two of the twelve sharing a silhouette at that size.

critique.observation: This is the strongest axis and the change is genuinely visible at 120px, which is where it counts. Across the states sheet the stress row is unmistakably the quiet row: white marks drop to a handful, and the blue beds multiply and run wider - 138, 175, 212 and 249 all gain several additional thin beds under stress and those beds extend closer to both frame edges. Recovery floods the bright strokes back in at higher density than neutral. Drawdown laying down more beds is delivered and it is legible.
critique.action: Two fixes. Recovery is claimed to rule bright lines through the whole field but delivers a starburst converging at a centre point, so make those recovery strokes span edge to edge at shallow angles rather than radiating from an interior origin. And seed 397 barely changes across all three states because it has almost no white layer to modulate; guarantee a minimum recovery seam count of 3-4 full-width rules for every seed so no token is state-blind.

critique.observation: Holds. Same seed across neutral, stress and recovery keeps its bed positions, its silhouette and its mass distribution - 138, 175 and 212 are obviously the same object three times. The weakest case is 101, where stress strips a dense tangle down to a bare X and the token nearly becomes a different work, though the underlying bar positions still identify it.
critique.action: Keep the current behaviour. When the white layer is cut per the palette note, hold the stress-state reduction ratio rather than the absolute count, so a high-density seed like 101 does not lose 80% of its marks in one state transition.

critique.observation: Named and located. Frame-edge clipping: 101 and 508 have white batons crossing all four edges and cut hard by the viewBox, and 360's fan is sliced flat at the left edge so it reads as a shape that has been chopped rather than one that continues. Collision mush: the centre of 101 neutral and 101 recovery, and the centre of 323, are a grey pile where individual strokes are no longer separable. Vanishing strokes: in 175 neutral and 471 the hairline white rules in the upper third fade to near-invisible against the darkest part of the ground. Overlap misread: the isolated bar at the very bottom of 175 neutral and 138 recovery sits below a gap and reads as a UI element rather than as part of the work.
critique.action: Inset the drawable region by about 4% and clip strokes to it so nothing terminates exactly on the frame boundary. Cap overlapping white strokes at 3 deep in any region and reduce per-stroke opacity to around 0.6 so crossings stay readable as separate lines. Set a minimum stroke luminance relative to the local ground so a rule on the dark upper field is lifted rather than swallowed. Remove the vertical gap above the lowest bed.
