The remaining four do not survive: 212 and 434 are both pairs of charcoal rectangles so close to the ground that they read as smudges with no internal event, and 101 and 471 both collapse to 'two tiny grey chips' and are interchangeable with each other. This is an improvement on round 1's five classes, but it is still not twelve, and the improvement came from the two-body arrangement that fails the brief -- so it will be spent when the second body is deleted.
critique.action: Raise the minimum fill luminance so 212 and 434 separate from the ground by at least 45%, and raise minimum slab area so 101 and 471 are no longer the smallest marks on the sheet. Then re-render contact-thumb.png with the single-body form and require all twelve neutrals to be individually nameable at 120px before tuning anything else.

critique.observation: Recovery has not been delivered at all. On states-thumb.png the stress row and the recovery row are the same row: I compared all twelve pairs -- 101, 138, 175, 212, 249, 286, 323, 360, 397, 434, 471, 508 -- and cannot distinguish a single one. Enlarging states.png confirms it at full size: 101 stress and 101 recovery carry the identical stepped dark bar at the lower block's bottom-left, and 212 stress and 212 recovery carry the identical 55x10 stub bar in the upper block. singles--seed175-stress.png and singles--seed175-recovery.png are the same picture pixel for pixel. The brief says 'Recovery should heal it'; nothing heals. In the other direction stress IS now visible at browse size on roughly seven of twelve (323, 360, 397, 508, 249, 138, 286 show clear dark seams at 120px), which is progress, but the mark reads as a bevel or a drop shadow rather than a crack because it hugs a block edge -- 175's seam sits about 4px below the cream block's top edge and 101's sits directly beneath the block as a detached plinth.
critique.action: Render recovery as a third distinct state, not a copy of stress: close the fissure to a 1-2px seam and restore about 70% of the cracked-open area to the stone fill, leaving the seam at a fixed value between stone and ground so a healed scar remains legible. Then require, as a build check, that every seed's recovery frame differs visibly from BOTH its neutral and its stress frame at 120px. Move the stress fissure off the edges: cut it through the slab's interior, crossing at least 60% of the slab's width, at 25-75% of its height.

critique.observation: This is the round's genuine repair and it should be protected. On states.png the four seeds shown (101, 138, 175, 212) hold their bounding boxes, centroids, aspect ratios and fill values constant across all three columns -- 212's lower block is byte-for-byte unchanged from neutral through recovery, and 175's cream and olive bodies stay at the same coordinates and the same tones in all three states. The round-1 failure where the slab was deleted and replaced by a re-proportioned, relocated, retoned object under drawdown is gone; you can now lay neutral over stress and see the same outline. The caution is that the fix has overshot into duplication: identity is being preserved by rendering the same picture twice.
critique.action: Keep the bounding-box, centroid and fill lock exactly as implemented, and add one constraint beside it: require a minimum pixel delta between stress and recovery (and between recovery and neutral) so that state identity cannot be satisfied by emitting an identical frame.

critique.observation: No clipping at the frame edge and nothing cut by the viewBox anywhere in the packet. But the stress marks still read as boolean accidents rather than as drawn marks. On states.png, 101's lower block has a dark bar occupying its bottom-left that leaves the block with a stepped, L-shaped silhouette -- the right end of the block hangs lower than the left -- and the same shape repeats in 101 recovery. 101's upper block has its dark bar sitting entirely BELOW the block rather than inside it, so it reads as a detached plinth or shadow, a third tone appended to the form. 212's stress mark is a stub bar roughly 55x10 that stops short of both the left and right edges of its block and reads as a smudge, not a fracture. 175's seams hug the top edge of one block and the bottom edge of the other, so both read as bevels.
critique.action: Draw every fissure as a full-width cut, edge to edge across the slab, at 2.5-3% of the slab's short dimension in thickness, and forbid any mark from being placed outside the parent slab's bounding box -- that removes 101's detached plinth. Snap fissure ends to the slab's own left and right edges so subtraction can only produce clean rectilinear splits, which removes 101's stepped silhouette and 212's floating stub.

critique.observation: Two of the brief's demands were met this round and three were not. Met: there is now exactly ONE body per token (the detached second rectangle that dominated round 2 is gone from all 12 cells of contact.png), and the forms are portrait rather than landscape. Not met, and this is the gate: the slab is not monumental, it is smaller than it has ever been. On contact.png every one of the twelve neutral forms measures exactly 32px tall in a 277px cell -- 11.5% of frame height, and identical for all twelve seeds. Round 1 measured this at 17%; the form has SHRUNK by a third while being told twice to grow. 'Upright' also still fails on five seeds: 249 is 30x32 (1.07:1, a square), 323 is 28x32, 360 is 28x32 and 508 is 28x32 (all 1.14:1), 138 is 24x32 (1.33:1). None reach the 1.4:1 asked in round 1 or the 1.6:1 asked in round 2. 'Two tones only' is broken in every frame but one. 'Recovery should heal it' has never been rendered in three rounds.
critique.action: Raise the slab height from the constant 32px to 165-190px in the 277px contact cell (60-70% of frame height, a 5x linear increase) and make height a per-seed variable instead of a constant. Clamp aspect to height/width >= 1.6:1 by REJECTING the draw and redrawing, not by squashing width: that cuts 249, 323, 360, 508 and 138 as currently generated. Set the slab base at 84-88% of frame height so it stands on the ground.

critique.observation: Across all 48 frames in the packet -- 12 on contact.png and 36 on states.png/states-thumb.png -- nothing touches an edge, nothing is cropped, there is no base, no horizon and no ground line. The slab's horizontal centre sits between 40% (212) and 56% (286) of cell width, so the placement jitter added this round is about +/-8% around dead centre and reads as wobble rather than as a decision. Worse, the base of the form sits at 55-64% of frame height on every seed, which puts MORE empty ground below the slab than above it: 249 and 323 have their base at 56% and 55%. The object therefore hovers in the upper middle of an even margin. With one small body and uniform void on four sides there is a focal subject by default but it commands nothing.
critique.action: Drop the base from 55-64% to a fixed 84-88% of frame height so the void becomes sky above a standing object rather than padding around a floating one. Let the slab's top cross the frame's top edge on roughly 3 of the 12 seeds so the frame crops the monument instead of containing it. Widen the horizontal jitter from the current +/-8% to the middle 40% of the frame, keyed to seed.

critique.observation: This is still the work's one intact strength and it survived a large structural change. Laid out on contact.png the twelve frames are unmistakably one project: the same near-black ground (RGB 17,17,17 on the top row, 14,14,13 on the bottom), the same flat unstroked axis-aligned fills, no gradient, no texture, no ornament, no stroke, the same silence. Nothing has been imported from another vocabulary and -- despite two rounds of the frame getting emptier -- nothing has been bolted on to compensate. The round-1 and round-2 warnings against buying variation with new mark types were both heeded.
critique.action: Hold this vocabulary fixed while executing the scale, aspect and value changes: keep the axis-aligned rectangle, the flat unstroked fill and the matte near-black ground exactly as they are, and buy every unit of new variation from slab proportion and seam POSITION rather than from any new mark type, gradient or hue.

critique.observation: The brief says two tones. Measured off contact.png the stone value is a continuous ramp from luminance 41 (286) to 199 (175) -- a 5x spread, which is jitter, not a chosen pair. Seven of twelve sit under 25% luminance separation from the ground: 286 at 9%, 434 at 11%, 360 at 12%, 249 at 13%, 212 at 18%, 471 at 19%, 508 at 23%. Round 1 asked for a 45% floor and round 2 asked for 45% specifically on 212 and 434; 434 is at 11%. On top of the ramp, third tones are now everywhere and there are MORE of them than in round 2, not fewer. Counting distinct fills inside the slab bbox: 101 neutral has 3 (ground 14, seam 113, stone 150); 175 neutral has 4 (14, 145, 176, 199); 101 stress has 4 (14, 31, 76, 150); 138 stress has 4 (14, 22, 32, 154); 175 stress has SIX (14, 92, 145, 153, 176, 199). Only 212 honours the brief, and only because it is a plain grey box with no mark in it at all.
critique.action: Collapse the ramp to ONE stone value -- pick 175's 199 -- and allow at most one second step at 80% of it (159). Enforce a hard floor of 45% luminance separation from the ground, which deletes 286, 434, 360, 249, 212, 471 and 508 as currently valued. Draw every seam and every stress mark in either the ground value or the stone value and nothing between: that removes the 113 on 101 neutral, the 145/176 on 175 neutral, the 31/76 on 101 stress and the 22/32 on 138 stress.

critique.observation: The slab HEIGHT is a constant, not a variable. Measured on contact.png it is exactly 32px on all twelve seeds, and on states.png it is exactly 32px on all twelve frames of all four seeds in all three states. The only geometric axis in the entire collection is width, which runs 16px (471) to 30px (249) -- a 14px spread. Beyond that the seeds differ only in fill lightness and in how many horizontal seams are drawn (212 has zero, 101 has one, 360 has four). Every form is an axis-aligned rectangle, horizontally near-centred, at the same height, with horizontal-only subdivision. This is one work at twelve settings, and it is narrower than round 2 was: the block-pair signature that made eight seeds nameable there was deleted and nothing was put in its place.
critique.action: Make height the primary seed variable and drive proportion across a real range -- 1.6:1 to 4.5:1 tall-and-narrow -- instead of holding height at 32px and varying width by 14px. Replace the seam COUNT axis with a seam POSITION axis: exactly one seam per token whose height travels from 15% to 85% up the slab across the seed range, running vertical on 2 seeds in 12. Cap total marks per token at 2, which cuts 360 from six marks to two.

critique.observation: Judged on contact-thumb.png at 120px only. Each form occupies between 9x15px (286, 434, 471) and 14x16px (249, 323, 360, 508) inside a 120px cell, so the whole collection is a field of 10-14 pixel marks. I can name three: 175 (the only bright cream chip on the sheet), 138 (the only one with legible striping), and 249 (the largest and darkest, nearly square). 286, 434, 471 and 360 are smudges I can barely separate from the ground. 101, 212, 323, 397 and 508 are interchangeable small grey rectangles -- I cannot tell which is which. That is three or four nameable classes out of twelve, against five in round 1 and eight in round 2. This is the sheet the rubric says decides everything, and it is the worst it has been.
critique.action: Do the scale and value work first and re-render this sheet before tuning anything else: raise the mark from 10-14px to 65-80px tall at 120px, and lift every fill to at least 45% luminance separation from the ground so 286, 434, 471 and 360 leave the smudge band. Then require, as a build check, that all twelve neutrals at 120px are individually nameable by silhouette alone before any other axis is touched.

critique.observation: Recovery has not been delivered, for the second round running, and this time it is provable rather than merely apparent. singles--seed175-stress.png and singles--seed175-recovery.png are the same file -- identical sha256 in REVIEW_REQUEST.json, and identical on screen. Aligning the form bounding boxes on states.png gives 0 differing pixels between stress and recovery on 101 (0 of 576), 138 (0 of 768), 175 (0 of 704) and 212 (0 of 640); the same test on states-thumb.png gives 0 differing pixels on ten of the twelve seeds, and the remaining two (360, 434) are visually identical. Nothing heals anywhere. In the other direction, two tokens do not respond to the market at all: 212's neutral, stress and recovery are 0 differing pixels from each other -- three identical frames -- and 286's neutral-to-stress maximum delta is 3 of 255, invisible. Of the ten seeds that do change, only 138, 175, 508 and 323 read as changed at 120px. Separately, the change that does occur is not the change the brief claims: on 101 stress the 'crack' is a solid 9x6 block at luminance 76 filling the bottom-right corner, and on 175 stress it is a band that darkens the top fifth. Those read as a shadow or a patch of different material, not as a fracture.
critique.action: Render recovery as a third distinct image: close the stress fissure to a 1-2px seam and restore about 70% of the cracked-open area to the stone value, leaving the healed seam at a fixed value between stone and ground. Add the build check round 2 asked for and did not get -- every seed's recovery frame must differ from BOTH its neutral and its stress frame by a minimum pixel delta at 120px, which would have failed this packet 12 times out of 12. Give 212 and 286 a stress mark at all. Re-cut the fracture as a ground-coloured fissure crossing at least 60% of the slab width at 25-75% of its height, replacing 101's corner block and 175's top band.

critique.observation: The bounding-box lock from round 2 held and should be protected. On states.png the stone bbox is byte-identical across all three states for every seed measured: 101 is 18x32 in neutral, stress and recovery; 138 is 24x32; 175 is 22x32; 212 is 20x32. Centroid, aspect and stone fill value are all constant through the row. You can lay neutral over stress and see the same outline, which was the round-1 catastrophe and is now genuinely fixed. But round 2 warned in writing that identity was being satisfied by duplication and asked for a minimum-delta constraint beside the lock. That constraint was not added, and the failure it predicted is now complete: 212 satisfies token identity by emitting the same picture three times.
critique.action: Keep the bbox, centroid and stone-value lock exactly as implemented, and add the second constraint beside it rather than instead of it: require each state to differ from the other two by at least 8% of the slab's pixel area while the bounding box stays fixed. That keeps 101's 18x32 outline constant and still forces 212 off its three identical frames.

critique.observation: Nothing is clipped by the viewBox and nothing collides into mush, but the marks still read as boolean and registration accidents rather than as drawn marks. Named and located: (1) 138 stress carries a stranded 2px-wide, 4px-tall patch of stone value 154 at x143-144, y141-144 -- a sliver left on the far right below the black bite, which reads as subtraction debris. (2) 138 neutral's two seams are staggered, one running from mid-slab to the right edge and one from the left edge to about 72%, so they read as two mis-registered bars rather than one seam; 249, 508 and 434 neutral repeat the same staircase pair. (3) 101 stress's mark is a filled block at luminance 76 pinned into the bottom-right corner touching both the bottom and right edges, which reads as a drop shadow, and its second mark is a 2px bar at luminance 31 flush with the top edge, which reads as a bevel. (4) 397 neutral has a luminance-83 band flush with the slab's top edge -- the same bevel read that round 2 flagged on 175. (5) 360 neutral carries four 2px seams at luminance 33-37 on a luminance-47 slab: 4-5% separation, invisible at 512px and absent at 120px, and six total marks on a token the brief caps at a handful.
critique.action: Snap every seam and fissure to the slab's own left and right edges so subtraction can only produce clean full-width rectilinear cuts -- that removes 138's stranded 154-value sliver and the staggered pairs on 249, 508 and 434. Forbid any mark from being placed within 10% of the slab's top or bottom edge, which removes 101's corner shadow and the bevel reads on 397 and 175. Require every internal mark to clear 25% luminance separation from its own slab fill, which deletes 360's four 33-37 seams outright, and cap marks per token at 2.
